![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14228741/assets/4ee9e02184efd314371a99c6242540e5e2e6effc9e21d41a86648b433b8a6938.png)

Consider the vector field $F(x,y)$ shown above. Let $C$ be the path where the semiellipse is traversed from $A$ to $B.$ Which of the following statements are true?

I. ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0$

II. ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0$

III. ${\int }_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0$
question.worked_solution:
Remember that ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r$ gives the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along $C:$

- If the force works *with* the motion of the particle (i.e., the force helps to push the particle along the path), then ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0.$

- If the force works *against* the motion of the particle (i.e., the force impedes the motion of the particle as it moves along the path), then ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0.$

With that in mind, let's check each statement.

- Statement I is true while statement II is false. It's clear from the picture below that $F$ assists the motion of the particle as it moves from $A$ to $B.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14228741/assets/1d91a85ccbb948e070db738373ffc5032f4e91a0ba8e04cd14e79276b0e798f8.png)

So, ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0.$

- Statement III is false. It's clear from the picture below that $F$ works against the motion of the particle as it moves from $B$ to $A.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14228741/assets/a8e0bffd04fb7b765d3c654f62b1958ab55a42f0d26cbc9f2b2e31f7d8e6f775.png)

So, ${\int }_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
